notes: Full test du 24/11 : « Sleep Tierlist For Optimal Health (Science based) », sa famille à 93 k (11/10) ; éléments à nous ; `source` gardée pour mémoire. Croquis de couverture neuf (sommeil.jpg, Seedream). Slide Atala (11) : le second A tier « Running During The Day », une coureuse de la banque et le logo d'Atala ; slide S en dernier. Texte selon placement_atala : voix TOUCHE PERSO (hook de 6 mots), un seul argument : écrire au coach / le plan s'adapte quand la semaine déborde ; version « cta F' ». Faits : écrans et lumière le soir retardent l'endormissement (Chang et al., PNAS 2015) ; la caféine a une demi-vie de plusieurs heures, 400 mg 6 h avant le coucher réduisent le sommeil (Drake et al., J Clin Sleep Med 2013) ; le décalage du week-end (« social jetlag », Wittmann et al. 2006) ; bain chaud 1 à 2 h avant le coucher et endormissement plus rapide (Haghayegh et al., Sleep Med Rev 2019) ; la baisse de température corporelle accompagne l'endormissement ; lumière du matin et horloge circadienne ; exercice régulier et meilleur sommeil (Kredlow et al., J Behav Med 2015), effort intense dans l'heure avant le coucher (Stutz et al. 2019).

paragraphes: Bright screens and endless feeds keep your brain alert right when it should be winding down.
You fall asleep later than you planned, and the sleep you do get is lighter.
Caffeine stays in your body for hours. An afternoon coffee is still working at bedtime.
You might still fall asleep, but your deep sleep pays.
Sleeping in for hours on the weekend shifts your body clock, like flying a few time zones every Friday.
Monday morning feels awful because your body thinks it's still the middle of the night.
It feels calmer than scrolling, but the screen keeps you alert and the next notification is one tap away.
Better than social media. Still not switching off.
A warm bath an hour or two before bed helps your body cool down after, which tells it to sleep.
Nice, and it helps a little. It can't fix a bad routine.
Bright lights at night tell your brain it's still daytime. Dimming them helps your body get ready for sleep.
Easy to do, but on its own it barely moves the needle.
Your body temperature has to drop for you to fall asleep. A cool, dark room makes that much easier.
Easy to fix, but it can't undo a day that fights sleep.
Your internal clock runs on rhythm. Going to bed at the same time makes it easier to fall asleep fast.
It misses A tier: your wake-up time matters most.
Bright light early in the day sets your internal clock, so you feel sleepy at the right time at night.
It only misses S tier because most people need a reason to go outside.
Regular exercise is linked to falling asleep faster and sleeping deeper, unless it's hard and late.
When my week gets busy, a running coach app like Atala adjusts my plan so I don't skip it.

en.nom: Waking Up At The Same Time
paragraphes: A fixed wake-up time anchors your whole rhythm: your energy, your hunger and when you get sleepy.
Every other habit on this list works better with it.
